candidate.answerReason: The four squares each have area 25 square centimeters and side length 5 centimeters. The figure has three shared sides, leaving ten square-side lengths on its boundary.

methods.label: Remove the shared sides
methods.explanation:
The four identical squares divide the total area equally, so each has area
\[
100\div4=25\text{ cm}^2.
\]
Since \(5\times5=25\), each square has side length \(5\text{ cm}\).

Adding the four squares' perimeters initially counts \(4\times4=16\) side lengths. In the figure, the two upper squares share one side, the two lower squares share one side, and the upper-right square shares one side with the lower-left square. These are all three shared sides.

Each shared side was counted twice, once for each square, but contributes nothing to the outer perimeter. Every other side belongs to the boundary and is counted once. Therefore the perimeter is
\[
(16-2\times3)\times5=10\times5=\boxed{50\text{ cm}},
\]
which is choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
methods.levelReason: Equal sharing of area, the square area formula, and counting exposed sides are elementary AMC 8 reasoning. Recognizing 25 as 5 times 5 avoids any need for formal square-root methods.
